United India Insurance Co.Ltd vs Ayisha on 6 February, 2025
Judgment
This appeal is filed by the 2 nd respondent insurance company in O.P.(MV) No. 191 of 2015 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kalpetta.

2. According to the appellant, the claim petitioner was a gratuitous passenger in the vehicle involved in the accident and he is not covered by the statutory policy issued by the insurance company and therefore, the company has no liability to pay compensation to the claim petitioner.
3.

At the time of occurrence, the claim petitioner was a passenger in the car driven by the 1 st respondent in a rash and negligent manner and the car caused to hit on the backside of a bus and overturned and thereby, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
4.
Before the Tribunal, Exhibits A1 to A6 and C1 were marked from the side of the petitioner and no evidence adduced from the side of the respondents.

As per the award dated 11.04.2017, the Tribunal arrived at a finding that the accident occurred because of the negligence on the part of the 1st respondent and that respondents 1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs. 45,150/- to the petitioner.

6. Subsequently, the insurance company filed I.A. No. 778 of 2017 seeking review of the award by producing the policy of insurance and contending that the policy issued is 'act only policy' and the company has no liability to pay compensation.

But, the Tribunal found that the company collected additional premium of Rs.175/- towards 'PA for unnamed persons' and in view of the additional premium collected, the company is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and hence, the review petition was dismissed.
7.

Heard Sri. T.V. Ajayakumar, the learned counsel for the appellant insurance company and Sri.
K.N. Rajani, the learned counsel for the 1st respondent.
8. As per the order in I.A. No. 1 of 2025, the policy of insurance is admitted as additional evidence in appeal and the same is marked as Exhibit B1.
The specific contention of the appellant is that Exhibit B1 is an 'act only policy' and the same will not cover the petitioner who was a 2025:KER:9793 gratuitous passenger in the private car.

The schedule of premium in Exhibit B1 shows that Rs.100/-
was collected towards 'compulsory PA for owner driver', Rs.175/- was collected for 'PA for unnamed persons' and Rs.50/- was collected towards 'LL to paid driver IMT 28'.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the respondent claim petitioner argued that in view of the additional premiums collected, the insurance company is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The learned counsel for the appellant argued that the additional premium was collected subject to IMT endorsements 16 and 28.

IMT endorsement 16 reads thus:
"IMT.16. Personal accident to unnamed passengers other than insured and the paid driver and cleaner (for vehicles rated as private cars and Motorised two wheelers (not for hire or reward) with or without side car)

In consideration of the payment of an additional premium it is hereby understood and agreed that the insurer undertakes to pay compensation on the scale provided below for bodily injuries hereinafter defined sustained by any passenger other than the insured and/or the paid driver attendant or cleaner and/or a person in the employ of the insured coming within the scope of the Workmens Compensation Act, 1923 and subsequent amendments of the said Act and engaged in and upon the 2025:KER:9793 service of the insured at the time of such injury is sustained whilst mounting into, dismounting from or travelling in but not driving the insured motor car and caused by violent, accidental, external and visible means which independently of any other cause shall within three calendar months of the occurrence of such injury result in:
 Details of injury Scale of  compensation  i) Death 100%
 ii) Loss of two limbs or sight or two eyes or one 100%
 limb and sight of one eye  iii) Loss of one limb or sight of one eye 50%
 iv) Permanent Total Disablement from injuries 100%
 other than named above  Provided always that (1)compensation shall be payable under only one of the items (I) to (iv) above in respect of any such person arising out of any one occurrence and total liability of the insurer shall not in the aggregate exceed the sum of Rs.3,50,000/- during any one period of insurance in respect of any such person.
(2) no compensation shall be payable in respect of death or injury directly or indirectly wholly or in part arising or resulting from or traceable to.
(a) Intentional self injury suicide or attempted suicide physical defect or infirmity or (b) an accident happening whilst such person is under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs.
(3)such compensation shall be payable only with the approval of the insured named i n t h e p o l i c y a n d d i r e c t l y t o t h e i n j u r e d p e r s o n o r h i s / h e r l e g a l representative(s)whose receipt shall be a full discharge in respect of the injury of such United India Insurance Co.Ltd vs Ayisha on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116198813/

Subject otherwise to the terms exceptions conditions and limitations of this policy."

10. Clause (iv) of the details of injury and scale of compensation and proviso 1 would show that in case of permanent total disablement from injuries other than mentioned in clauses (i) to (iii), the liability is 100%, subject to the limit prescribed in the first proviso that the total liability of the insurer shall not in the aggregate exceed the sum of Rs.3,50,000/- during any one period of insurance in respect of any such person.

11. In this case, the total compensation awarded by the Tribunal is only Rs.45,150/- and therefore, in view of the additional premiums collected, the appellant insurance company is liable to pay compensation to the claim petitioner subject to the limit as per IMT endorsement 16.
For the aforesaid reasons, I find no merit in the appeal and hence the appeal is liable to be dismissed.
In the result, this appeal is dismissed.
